description: Key facts for the Kingdom chapter: written by hand from the reviewed chapter text. Every entry links to the section that explains it.

people.name: Romulus
people.text: Legendary founder and first king of Rome; chose the first hundred senators.

people.name: Remus
people.text: Romulus's twin brother, killed after the two quarrelled over founding their city.

people.name: Rhea Silvia
people.text: Vestal Virgin and mother of the twins, a princess of Alba Longa.

people.name: Numa Pompilius
people.text: The peaceful second king; founded the Vestal Virgins and, legend says, added January and February.

people.name: Tullus Hostilius
people.text: The warlike third king; destroyed Alba Longa and built the senate house, the Curia Hostilia.

people.name: Ancus Marcius
people.text: Fourth king; founded the port of Ostia and built the first bridge over the Tiber, the Pons Sublicius.

people.name: Tarquinius Priscus
people.text: The first Etruscan king; built the Cloaca Maxima and the Circus Maximus and held the first triumph.

people.name: Servius Tullius
people.text: Sixth king; held the first census and sorted citizens into five classes by wealth.

people.name: Tarquin the Proud
people.text: Tarquinius Superbus, the seventh and last king, remembered as a tyrant.

people.name: Lucretia
people.text: Noblewoman whose rape by the king's son and her death sparked the uprising against the kings.

people.name: Lucius Junius Brutus
people.text: The king's nephew who led the revolt; one of Rome's first two consuls.

people.name: Lars Porsenna
people.text: Etruscan king of Clusium who marched on Rome to bring Tarquin back.

people.name: Horatius Cocles
people.text: Hero who, legend says, held the Pons Sublicius alone until it could be torn down.

dates.text: Possible first traces of settlement on the Capitoline Hill.
The traditional founding of Rome, celebrated on 21 April; Romans counted years from it.
A wall is built on the Palatine Hill.
The villages have become a city, with a forum, monumental buildings and temples.
Tarquin the Proud is expelled; two consuls are elected and the Republic begins.
Rome defeats an alliance of Latin towns at Lake Regillus.
Tarquin dies in exile at Cumae.
The Gauls sack Rome, destroying many early records.
Fabius Pictor writes the first history of Rome, in Greek.
